segments: The hundred and fifteenth cycle.
Arab Kings.
And Anastasius reigned two years and five months.
Now Walid was a great hater of the Christians;
and as for the great church of the Greeks in Damascus, which the Arabs had seized and in exchange for which they gave a site where the new church of the Mother of God was built,
he changed the structure of that former church,
and built it into a great and famous mosque.
And he also commanded that the Christian notaries should no longer write the accounts of the treasury in Greek,
but in Arabic.
And Walid said to Sham'ala, the chief of the Taghlibite Christian Arabs:
"Since you are the chief of the Arabs,
you bring shame upon all of them
by worshipping the Cross.
Therefore, do my will
and become a Muslim."
But he replied:
"For this reason,
because I am the head of all the Taghlibites,
I fear lest I become the cause of destruction to all of them, if I deny, and they deny, the Christ."
Now when Walid heard these things,
he commanded, and they dragged him upon his face and cast him out.
And he sent to him with oaths,
that if he did not submit,
he would feed him his own flesh.
Yet even so he did not weaken.
And he commanded, and they cut a piece of flesh from his thigh,
and roasted it in the fire,
and cast it into his mouth.
And when he endured firmly against this as well,
he let him be.
And he remained alive, while that scar could be seen in his flesh.
And he also commanded that the sorcerers in the region of 'Aqula be put to death.
And when they were bound and tied to pieces of wood,
so that they might not perish quickly,
they were cast into the river.
And those who floated, they killed,
because by their sorceries, so it was said, they floated.
And those who sank,
they pulled out and let go.
And he also commanded,
Walid,
and Christian captives were slain inside the churches in all the cities of Syria.
And in the year 1026,
(1026 of the Greeks?) Walid died.
[reigned] after [him?] ... months {OCR?}.
At the beginning of his reign,
Maslama fought and captured a fortress in the country of Galatia,
and he returned with much plunder.
And the army which Anastasius had sent to the west rebelled,
and killed their commander,
and brought Theodosius,
and he reigned for one year.
And Anastasius fled to Nicaea.
And in the year 1026,
